name: Healthy baby hair
tagline: A guide to looking after your edges.
image_alt: A woman with long dark curls presses her fingertips along her hairline and side part.
description: What wears edges down, a weekly routine, styles that give them a break, and what to look for on a label.
intro: The hair at your hairline is the finest hair on your head. It breaks first and grows back slowest. This guide covers what wears edges down, what to do each week, and what to look for on a label.

causes.title: Why edges get thin
causes.intro: Most thin edges come from the same few things. Often more than one at a time.
items: Tight braids, ponytails and buns. Wigs with tight bands or glue. This is the most common cause, and the one you have the most say over.
The hair is held under tension for hours or days at a time.
Cotton pillowcases. Scarves, hats and wig caps that sit right on the hairline. Headbands you wear every day.
Friction wears the hair down until it snaps.
Brushing edges down over and over, with a stiff brush and a hard-hold gel.
It pulls the same short hairs in the same direction, every day.
Relaxers, color, bleach and flat irons near the front.
The hair there is fine to begin with, so it takes the damage first.
Edges dry out faster than the rest of your hair, and dry hair snaps more easily.
They are exposed, and they are usually the last place anyone moisturizes.
Thyroid trouble, low iron, pregnancy, menopause, some illnesses and some medicines can all thin hair.
A routine cannot fix these. A doctor can look into them.

stock.title: Before you start
stock.intro: Write these down today, with photos. Check the same list at week 4 and week 8. That is how you will know whether anything changed.
items: Front, left temple, right temple. Same light, same angle, same hair state each time.
Where they are full, where they are thin, where you see short broken hairs.
Comfortable, dry, flaky, itchy, sore or red.
The styles you have worn in the last month, and how long each one stayed in.
Your pillowcase, bonnet, scarf, hat, headband, wig cap.
Your cleanser, conditioner, leave-in, gel, edge control, oil or serum.

routine.title: Your routine
routine.intro: Five steps on wash day. A few small things the rest of the time.

wash.title: Your wash day
steps: Wash your scalp. Go gently at the front, and let the suds rinse down the lengths on their way out.
Deep conditioner or rinse-out, whichever you are using that day. Work it through your edges too, not only the lengths.
On your edges as well. This is the slip that stops styling from tugging at them later.
Once your scalp is dry. Daily, or as often as the label says.
Nothing pulling at the front. There are eight to choose from below.

between.title: Between wash days
groups: Check for soreness, itching or redness.
Put on your scalp serum. Daily, or as often as the label says.
Pick a style that does not pull at your temples.
Loosen anything that got tight during the day.
Silk or satin: bonnet, scarf or pillowcase.
No tight bands sitting on your hairline.
A second serum only if the label asks for one.

weeks.title: A different style each week
weeks.intro: Edges need a break from tension. Here is one style to try each week, so you are not wearing the same pull for eight weeks. Swap them around to suit you.
items: Chunky, and started a little back from your hairline.
Tied with a soft scrunchie, not a thin elastic.
Edges left exactly as they dry.
The same style you like, in a larger size, taken out sooner.
Tied behind your ears, not across your hairline.
Nothing gripping the front at all.
Parted so the tension sits on the top of your head, not the edge.
A wig day, or a hair-down day
Adjustable cap, no glue, no tight band. Or nothing at all.

use.title: What to use
use.intro: Products by the job they do in this routine. Choose your own brands; these are the jobs to fill.
items: Keeps the scalp clean, so your serum lands on skin instead of buildup.
The step where the growth-focused ingredients go.
Daily, or as the label says
Softens the fine hair at your hairline, so it bends instead of snapping.
Slip, so styling does not tug at the front.
Every wash, and when you restyle
Keeps your edges from drying out between washes.
A little, when they feel dry
Edge control, if you use one
Soft hold. Hard-hold gels dry stiff and crack the hair they are holding.
Stops your pillow rubbing your edges all night.

choose.title: One serum, or more than one?
choose.intro: Different serums do different things, so there is a real case for using more than one. There is also a cost to it. Here is how the three choices actually play out.
items: Give it the full eight weeks before you judge it. One product at a time is the only way to know which one your scalp liked, which one it did not, and what to buy again.
One in the morning and another at night, or one on wash day and another midweek. This suits a scalp that gets irritated easily, and it still lets you tell the two apart.

Both in the same sitting, thinnest first, letting each one soak in before the next. It makes sense when they do different jobs: say, a water-based serum for the scalp and an oil to seal moisture at the hairline.

Two products built on the same active. You are not doubling anything, you are paying twice. And do not start a new serum in the same week you change your cleanser or your style; if something reacts, you will not know what caused it.

ing.title: What to look for if you are trying to grow your edges back
ing.intro: These ingredients show up in scalp serums most often, but also in scalp oils and sprays, in some shampoos and conditioners, and in a few greases and edge controls. The ingredient list on the back is what tells you, not the words on the front.
items: Studied in lab-grown hair follicles. Interesting, early, and not the same as a serum regrowing edges on a person.
The most-studied of these. A 2025 review of nine studies found the results leaned positive, but most of the studies were weak.
Different blends do different things. Each one has to be judged on its own research, not on the word peptide.
A well-established skin ingredient. It conditions the scalp; it is not a growth treatment on its own.
Softens the hair and improves how it feels.
The slip in your conditioner. Less friction when you comb means less breakage.
They sit on the surface and slow water loss. That is moisture kept in, not growth.

trouble.title: If something feels off
items: Your scalp is sore after a style
It is too tight. Take it down. Soreness is not something to get used to.
A new serum makes you itch, flake or go red
Stop it. Go back to what you were using. Try something else after a week or two.
Your edges feel dry and crunchy
Look at your gel or edge control first, then add a moisturizer at the hairline.
You keep finding short broken hairs
Check friction and brushing before you buy anything new.
Eight weeks in, nothing has changed
That is worth a dermatologist's time, not another product.

end.title: See a dermatologist if
notes: Hair lost to years of pulling can stop coming back. The earlier someone looks at it, the more options you have.
list: Your hairline is moving back, or keeps getting thinner.
You see smooth, shiny patches where the skin looks different.
Hair is coming out in patches.
end.source: American Academy of Dermatology: Hairstyles that pull can lead to hair loss
